subject: SpectraWorks: downstream rights, training opt-out & feedback license — checklist
messages:
From: Ella Morris <ella.morris@spectraworks.com>
To: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com
Cc: legal@spectraworks.com, tom.brooks@spectraworks.com
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on rights language in draft MSA

Hi Mateo —

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. Our legal team reviewed the draft MSA and Order Form and surfaced three items we need clarified before procurement can sign: (1) explicit downstream productization rights (we want to confirm whether output is assignable or licensed), (2) an opt-out path for model training using our data, and (3) a narrow feedback license — ideally limited to safety/quality improvements only.

I attached the redline from our counsel (high level) — can you confirm how Redwood typically handles each of these in the hosted vs dedicated deployment models? If possible, provide an internal checklist of evidence we should expect for any ownership/assignment ask.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — we aim to finalize commercial terms by end of next week.

Best,
Ella Morris
Head of Product, SpectraWorks

Attachment: SpectraWorks_MSA_comments.pdf (stub)

From: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com
To: Ella Morris <ella.morris@spectraworks.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on rights language in draft MSA

Hi Ella —

Thanks for the note and the redline. High-level answers here, then I’ll loop in Laura (legal) and Ben (solutions/ops) for details and an evidence checklist.

1) Output ownership: Our standard position is to license output to customers for their internal and commercial uses; assignment of title is uncommon but we can discuss limited carveouts. For dedicated/private customers we can discuss stronger exclusivity terms subject to procurement/price adjustments.

2) Training opt-out: We offer an explicit opt-out flag at the account level for Hosted API customers (no customer data used for model training/continuous improvements). For Dedicated/Private deployments, customer data never leaves the customer-controlled environment; nevertheless we still include a feedback license to allow improvements to the Redwood platform unless specifically carved out.

3) Feedback license: We can accept a narrow, purpose-limited feedback license that excludes using customer-provided prompts/outputs for model training; the language needs to be scoped to (a) aggregated telemetry for safety, (b) anonymized metrics, and (c) excludes reproducible prompt-output pairs for supervised training.

I’ve attached the draft redline from our side (MSA_redline_v3) and an initial list of evidence items procurement usually requests. Laura — can you review the proposed carve language and confirm the recommended wording? Ben — FYI on ops requirements for the opt-out flag and evidence runbook.

Thanks,
Mateo Alvarez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: SpectraWorks_MSA_redline_v3.docx; evidence-checklist.xlsx

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com, Ella Morris <ella.morris@spectraworks.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 8 Jun 2026 08:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on rights language in draft MSA

Ella / Mateo —

Read through Mateo’s draft redline. Below are suggested edits that we believe strike the right balance between SpectraWorks’ productization needs and our platform/OSS exposure:

- Output license clause: Replace 'assigns all output' with 'grants customer a perpetual, worldwide, transferable license, subject to Service-specific use restrictions' — this preserves strong customer rights while avoiding assignment language that raises IP transfer issues.

- Training opt-out clause: Add a one-sentence opt-out mechanism: 'Customer may elect, via account setting or written notice, to exclude Customer Data from Redwood model training and continuous improvement programs.' Also include a 30-day processing window and an audit trail for the change.

- Feedback license: Add explicit prohibitions: 'Redwood shall not use Customer Content or Prompt-Output Pairs for model training or to improve generative quality. Redwood may use anonymized telemetry and aggregated metrics for safety, performance, and infrastructure improvements.'

I will prepare a tracked-change version of the MSA and a short summary memo for procurement. Ben — I'll need you to confirm the operational feasibility of (a) the opt-out flag timeline and (b) the audit logs we can provide.

Laura Bennett
Sr. Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, mateo_alvarez@redwood.com, Ella Morris <ella.morris@spectraworks.com>
Date: Tue, 8 Jun 2026 11:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on rights language in draft MSA

Quick ops note — we can implement the opt-out flag for Hosted API accounts. Implementation details:
- Turnaround: 5 business days to fully ensure exclusion from downstream training pipelines once opt-out is set; we’ll annotate in logs.
- Evidence: Provide an audit export (CSV) showing the opt-out activation timestamp + ingestion/processing markers.
- For Dedicated: confirm we will set 'training=false' at the cluster/tenant level; no upstream replication to Redwood-managed training datasets.

I attached a sample evidence checklist (evidence-checklist.xlsx) — shows what procurement normally asks: access logs, KV cache retention, telemetry sample, and a signed statement from infra that data is segregated.

Ben Carter
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference

From: Ella Morris <ella.morris@spectraworks.com>
To: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com
Cc: legal@spectraworks.com, tom.brooks@spectraworks.com
Date: Wed, 9 Jun 2026 09:41:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on rights language in draft MSA

Thanks — this is helpful. A few follow-ups from our counsel: (1) the license needs to be explicit that customer may sublicense downstream (we're a platform vendor and often redistribute outputs to our end-customers), (2) the opt-out processing window of 5 business days is acceptable but procurement wants a fallback if opt-out fails (e.g., credit or contract remedy), and (3) they want sample log exports before signature to validate format.

Can you provide: a short sentence for sublicensing permission, a one-paragraph fallback remedy for opt-out failure, and a sanitized sample of the audit export? If we can get those by end of Thursday (June 10), we can keep the signature target.

Thanks,
Ella

From: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com

Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com

Laura & Ben have confirmed the language and evidence format.

Next steps: If SpectraWorks legal is comfortable with the attached MSA_redline_v3, we'll move the Order Form to signature and coordinate procurement evidence exchange via the Drive link.

Appreciate the partnership — looking forward to getting SpectraWorks live.

Best,
